name: Tahath
overview: Tahath was a male descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, identified explicitly as a son of Ephraim in 1 Chronicles 7:20. His lineage presents a challenge as the linear genealogy from Ephraim to Joshua contains too many generations when including Tahath. He is noted to have been killed by the men of Gath.
namesAndTitles: The name Tahath is a proper name meaning "compensation." It was not given by God but is recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:20. This name is the only one associated with him in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tahath as a son of Ephraim, and it is inferred that Eleadah was his father. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are detailed.
scriptureSignificance: Tahath's significance lies in his place within the Ephraimite genealogy, which is important for understanding the lineage leading to Joshua. The mention of his death at the hands of the men of Gath highlights the ongoing conflicts experienced by the tribe of Ephraim. His presence in the genealogical record helps trace the history and challenges of the Ephraim tribe during the period recorded in 1 Chronicles.
